q: Our motor buyer wants the carbon footprint of the rare earth magnets we buy from Baotou. What do we ask?
title: Carbon data for Baotou rare earth magnets
short: Ask the magnet maker for a cradle to gate footprint per kilogram covering separation, metal making, alloy casting and sintering, with the electricity source. Magnets are not CBAM goods, so this is a footprint request; if no figure comes, label any estimate clearly.
audience: Motor and EV component makers buying NdFeB magnets from Baotou and Inner Mongolia

ul: Rare earth separation, which uses chemicals and heat.
Metal production by electrolysis, which uses a lot of electricity.
Alloy casting, milling, sintering and heat treatment of the magnets.
Footprint per kilogram of magnet, with the system boundary stated.
Electricity used per kilogram and where it came from.
Which stages it runs itself and which it buys in.

sections.h: If the supplier has no figure
p: Use a published estimate for the material and mark it as secondary data. Keep asking: magnets can be a large share of a motor's footprint, and buyers increasingly expect primary data.

senseible: Senseible reads supplier invoices into dated, fingerprinted records, so each purchased material in a Scope 3 figure traces back to its document.
